Doctor of Philosophy in Energy and Environment
Programme

能源及環境哲學博士

Doctor of Philosophy
哲學博士

School of Energy and Environment
Mode of Study
Full-time
Part-time
Credit Units Required for Graduation
14 & SG8001
Programme Aims
This programme aims to provide students with a broad knowledge and skill set in the area of energy and environmental science, enabling them to create new knowledge, develop innovative technologies and to conduct problem-focused research as an internationally successful scientist.
Programme Intended Learning Outcomes (PILOs)
Upon successful completion of this Programme, students should be able to:
1. design and conduct experiments relevant to energy and/or the environment, as well as to critically analyze and interpret the experimental results
2. develop new concepts and innovative approaches to solve environmental and/or energy related problems
3. apply their acquired analytical and problem solving skills in an open-minded creative way so that they can adapt to an international work environment in their later career, and to communicate and work efficiently in a team
Programme Requirements
Research Area(s) in which research students will be admitted to:
Environmental Science, Energy and Built Environment; Materials Science and Engineering; Sustainable Manufacturing; Electronic Engineering; Bioengineering, Molecular and Life Science; Applied Mathematics
Programme Core Courses: [ 5 + 6 (from belonging stream, refer to remarks of elective) credits]
Course Code Course Title Credit Units
SEE8003 Skills for Scientists 2
SEE8212 Data Analysis in Environmental Applications 3
Research Methodology and Ethics Course(s):
Nil
Programme Electives: (3 credits)
Please refer to the updated list of approved courses for research students posted in the SGS website.
Other Requirement (not counted towards the University coursework requirement):
Course Code Course Title Credit Units Remarks
SG8001 Teaching Students: First Steps 1
- Collaborative Institutional Training Initiative (CITI) programme - An online training course on research integrity. Compulsory for RPg students who admitted in 2018/19 and thereafter. To be completed in the first year of study. Details are available in SGS website.
Qualifying Examination (for PhD only):
Compulsory written exam.
PhD students can sit in the qualifying examination for 2nd time if they fail to pass in the first trial.
PhD students will choose one of the three specific streams of expertise for QE according to the nature of their research (i.e. (i) sustainability, (ii) energy and (iii) environment)
Qualifying/Annual Report Submission:
Students must pass the annual assessment, which is consist of (i) submission of progress report and (ii) oral presentation followed by Q&A by panel
